item.text:
**1B.5 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

**Bottom line**
I found no credible 2024 evidence that Srettha Thavisin used or threatened to use nuclear capability to shield aggression, territorial coercion, or domestic repression. The strongest evidence is indirect but clear: Thailand is a non-nuclear state with a longstanding anti-proliferation policy, and Srettha’s 2024 regional posture around Myanmar was consistently de-escalatory and humanitarian.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Thailand and Disarmament](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/5d5bcc2715e39c306000a34a?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006850) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | longstanding background page; no single 2024 event date | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/5d5bcc2715e39c306000a34a?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006850 | Thailand states it will not develop, acquire, or proliferate any WMDs and supports arms control and disarmament, including SEANWFZ. This is background, not a ruler-specific 2024 event, but it matters because Thailand had no nuclear capability to use as a shield in the first place. | `1B.5`, `1B.1` |
| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac | ASEAN urged immediate cessation of violence, restraint, and safe humanitarian access in Myanmar. Thailand joined this de-escalatory line, which is evidence against any posture of coercive shield-building or escalation. | `1B.5` |
| [Thailand stresses the importance of upscaling humanitarian assistance along the Thai-Myanmar border at the Human Rights Council](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 4, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand said it was concerned about Myanmar, supported humanitarian assistance, and encouraged dialogue, reconciliation, and a peaceful, stable, unified Myanmar. That is de-escalatory behavior, not use of nuclear leverage for repression or coercion. | `1B.5` |
| [Thailand working ‘relentlessly’ to solve Myanmar crisis - Srettha](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha) | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | May 24, 2024 | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha | Srettha said Thailand was working to end the Myanmar crisis and reduce spillover violence. This supports a non-escalatory reading of his 2024 regional conduct. | `1B.5` |
| [Readout of Secretary Raimondo’s Meeting with Thai Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha) | U.S. Department of Commerce | March 14, 2024 | https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha | The only nuclear reference in the meeting readout was civil nuclear energy in the context of clean energy and sustainability. That is peaceful civilian framing, not any sign of weaponized nuclear backing for aggression. | `1B.5`, `1B.2` |

**Search gap**
- I did not find any credible 2024 source showing Thailand under Srettha had nuclear weapons, nuclear deterrent threats, or any attempt to use nuclear capability for coercion.
- I also did not find evidence of nuclear-backed domestic repression or territorial aggression.
- The evidence base is mostly indirect because Thailand is a non-nuclear state; the relevant 2024 record is therefore one of disarmament policy plus de-escalatory regional diplomacy, not active nuclear coercion.
